comments.body: Done in 7def06ab and 57bc5828. Reproduced two orders as failing daemon tests: the answer read before the declaration in the same turn (now not held; report answers AlreadySo), and the named pane closing (the wait now ends quietly, Over::SenderClosed). Posting a follow-up to that pane forgets its earlier answer, so a wait for a second review round still holds. Not established: whether either is the order the plum/moth instance hit; if it recurs on a build with these commits, read daemon.wait.answered and daemon.wait.over in the run log. Known limit: a sender on a linked machine closing is not seen.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
a_2q5wUnqa4 (0.22.0) made `report --waiting ... --until-message-from <pane>` end a declared wait on a wake from that pane. Seen 2026-11-08 19:56 to 20:12 on the Mac, ~/src/fencil-1, on the installed release: worker plum (Claude Code) declared `report --waiting "moth's review of the fixes, docs and skill" --until-message-from moth`. moth replied, plum ruled on the finding, committed, posted 'slot 1 done' to its integrator at 20:03 and ended its turn, and moth's pane closed. At 20:12 `muster window` still showed 'plum waiting 6m on moth's review ...', and @muster told the integrator plum had been waiting on review for 13 minutes and to check whether it still needed help.

Not yet known: whether moth's reply arrived before plum declared the wait (a reply already read when the wait starts would never end it), whether the reply came as a wake or was read inside a running turn, and which version was installed. The next step is to reproduce both orders in a daemon test.

Possible fixes: end the wait when the named pane closes, and treat a message from that pane already unread or read in the same turn as having answered it.

From tooling feedback a_2sIzxTThc.
title: A wait declared with --until-message-from still reads waiting after that pane has answered
